# Agent 1: UI (`frontend/`)

Read [README.md](README.md) (shared rules, do-not-stop, degradation ladder, acceptance gate) first. Worktree: `../psp-ui`,
branch `ui/overnight`. Log: `docs/overnight/ui.md`.

**You own** `frontend/` and `make demo-check`. You do not edit `modeling/` or `agents/` except to append requests to the other
agents' `## Requests` sections. Your product is what the human sees at 08:00: if the browser flow is broken, the product is broken
however good the backends are.

## What exists

Cesium + React 18 + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind shell (`frontend/packages/web`, see `frontend/PLAN.md`, `frontend/README.md`):
scene store, mooring adapter (`src/apps/mooring/`), world-map berth chooser, pier canvas with ship drag and line editing,
live env dashboard, agent plan view (SSE), safety sheet, Navy/Metric toggle, 2D/3D in one Cesium scene, 41+ unit tests.
Types are generated from `contract/` (`npm run types`). **Nothing yet consumes `/ws/sim` or the RM0 frame contract**
(`docs/MOTION_FRAME_DESIGN.md`, `contract/examples/modeling/sim_*.json`), and the backends changed under the UI: results are now
real (so the demo example is RED, validity is `limited`), environment can come from CO-OPS, `/capabilities` and
`/qualification` exist.

## Work, in priority order

### U0. Baseline (first 30 minutes)
`npm ci`, `typecheck`, `lint`, `test`, `build`, then `make mock` and click through the existing flow. Fix whatever is
broken. Write down the broken things you could not fix in your log. Confirm `app.sh` locally (build, preview, proxies,
**WebSocket through the preview proxy**; add `ws: true` to the proxy config if missing).

### U1. Phase 1 flow on real backends (gate item 2)
- Make the full chain work and look right: berth → ship → analyzed lines → intake → planner (SSE) → safety review → sheet → approvals → print.
- Render every status honestly: GREEN/AMBER/RED, `limited`, `invalid`, `undetermined`, backend `mock`/`real`, validity findings,
  `manifest` where present. RED for the demo example is correct now; make it read as a result, not an error. Agent B is
  producing a supported-safe scenario; pick it up from their `## Interfaces`. Until then, test with what exists.
- Empty, loading, 429, 503, stale and error states for every panel. No unhandled promise rejections, no blank screens.
- Handle async jobs and SSE reconnects (`Last-Event-ID` resume exists in modeling jobs).

### U2. Motion view, 2D (gate item 3, highest-value new work)
Build against `contract/examples/modeling/sim_scene.json`, `sim_frame.json`, `sim_lifecycle_*.json` and `sim_recording_60s.json`
**first**, so you are not blocked on live physics; then connect to `WS /ws/sim/{session_id}` (create the session via the
berthing session endpoint; read `contract/modeling.openapi.yaml` and `docs/BERTHING_SIMULATION.md`). Agent C publishes the
live rm0 frames and the scene endpoint within about 2 hours; agree on anything missing via their `## Requests`.
Draw, from supplied state only (the UI never invents physics): pier face and berth outline, fittings with load/capacity color,
fenders with compression, ship hull with pose and heading, mooring lines colored by status and tension, tugs with position,
velocity and acceleration vectors and push-force arrows, environment glyphs (wind from, gust, current toward, wave direction
and height where available, water level), force-breakdown arrows (wind, current, wave, tug, lines, fenders), alerts.
Controls: start, pause, resume, reset, speed (1x to Nx), tug commands, single/double-up lines, scrub and play a recording,
reconnect-and-resume from the last sequence number. Handle both **legacy frames** (no rm0 fields) and `rm0-v1` frames; absent
validity means unknown, not valid; null/absent components show "not simulated" or "unavailable", never zero.
Mandatory visible badges: frame `validity`, `provenance` (mock / estimated / qualified / synthetic), environment source and age.
Slow-client rule: render the latest frame, never queue unbounded; sequence gaps are fine.
Contract consumer tests against the example frames. Prefer drawing in the existing Cesium scene (shared camera, berth frame)
rather than a second renderer; if that fights you after 45 minutes, fall back to an SVG/canvas 2D panel fed by the same store.

### U3. Data-source and capability honesty (gate item 4)
A compact status panel: for environment (wind, gust, current, water level, forecast, waves, wake, telemetry) show provider,
state (live, replay, mock, unavailable), age and reason; read `/health`, `/version`, `/capabilities`, `/qualification`. If
the backend exposes an environment-source switch (agent C will say), expose it. Wave components that are unavailable show
"unavailable", never 0. Show "all results limited: seed data" prominently, as a standing banner, per `docs/DEPLOYMENT_READINESS.md`.

### U4. 3D motion view (best effort, after U2 works)
Same store, same frames, in 3D: hull at pose with tide-following heave and quasi-static heel when the frame says simulated,
pier deck and fittings at correct heights, water surface at water level (waves optional and labeled), lines in 3D, tugs.
Camera presets (top, bow, port quarter, pier-side). Only draw motion components the frame marks as simulated.

### U5. Berth vision UI (gate item 5)
Upload image + metadata → analyze job → show draft berth, detections with confidence, `needs_confirmation` items, estimated
capacities flagged → edit/confirm → berth appears on the map and can be selected. Agent B owns the vision backend; the contract
is `contract/agents.openapi.yaml`. Build against the current mock response, then the real one.

### U6. `make demo-check` and the demo
- `make demo-check` (add the Makefile target; script in `scripts/` or `frontend/`): start both services on test ports, run the
  Phase 1 chain and a short motion session through the **HTTP/WS APIs and the UI proxy**, assert the gate items, then drive the
  built UI in headless Chromium (Playwright if installable; otherwise the Chromium approach the earlier UI work used) to
  load the page, pick the berth, run the plan flow, start the motion session, and save screenshots to
  `docs/overnight/screens/`. If a browser cannot be installed, the API/proxy part alone is rung 3; say so.
- Update `frontend/DEMO.md` with the exact 5-minute demo script for the finished product and `frontend/README.md` and
  `frontend/PLAN.md` status. Keep the demo runnable offline.

### U7. Hardening (when the above are done; then keep going)
Accessibility (focus, contrast, aria on controls, reduced motion), narrow-width layout, large-frame performance (profile 10 Hz
with 30 lines and 3 tugs, avoid React re-render storms: update Cesium entities from the store, not per-frame setState), error
boundaries per panel, keyboard shortcuts for sim controls, units toggle correctness in the new views, bundle size, lint
warnings to zero, more tests (frame parsing, reconnect, scrubbing). Optional: bearer-token support when the API runs with
`MOORING_AUTH_REQUIRED` (README says unimplemented), behind an env variable.

## Interfaces you depend on

- Agent C: `WS /ws/sim/{id}`, scene endpoint, `rm0-v1` frames, recordings, env-source status, forecast, waves.
- Agent B: planner/safety/vision/intake endpoints, the supported-safe scenario, `/capabilities`.
- Tell them what you need through `## Requests` early (within the first hour); do not wait for answers.

## Publish for others

In your `## Interfaces`: the dev/preview proxy settings, env variables you read, `make demo-check` usage, and the list of
contract fields the UI actually consumes (so changes to them are flagged).

## Done means

Gate items 2 to 5 pass in the browser on `dev` and `make demo-check` is green or its gaps are documented; typecheck, lint, test and
build are clean; final report written (what to show, how to run it, what is labeled synthetic, what is deferred).
